content.title: Identity Board Verification | Action and Camera Changes Preserve Identity
content.summary: The fixed character board continues at the bottom of the screen, and the upper live-action area proves the same character with different motion profiles, distances, camera positions, and later skills; as a new source of evidence for the existing character card verification template, no new drop-down items are added.

quick_start.input_format: Fixed character board + same original subject + at least 4 different verification responsibilities + wide-angle/close-up dual proof + final comparison
quick_start.recommended_input: The fixed felt zero-gravity archivist identity board remains unchanged, and the live-action area above sequentially verifies the hatch posture, star chart tool, magnetic shoe gait, goggle reaction and a floating wax seal capture; only as an evidence variation of the existing character board template.
required_anchors: Keep one compact identity board unchanged and readable throughout.
Verify the same subject across at least three different live-view scales or poses.
Preserve key identity anchors through camera-angle and motion changes.
Reserve one late complex skill proof and hold it beside the unchanged board.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: The fixed character board continues at the bottom of the screen, and the upper live-action area proves the same character with different motion profiles, distances, camera positions, and later skills; as a new source of evidence for the existing character card verification template, no new drop-down items are added.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one compact identity board visually unchanged while a separate live area verifies the same subject through several functionally different proofs. Vary pose, distance, camera angle and movement silhouette, then reserve one late high-complexity skill proof; the board is a continuous comparison standard, not decoration.

invariants.rule: Keep one compact identity board unchanged and readable throughout.
invariants.ablation_failure: A changing board removes the comparison standard.

invariants.rule: Verify the same subject across at least three different live-view scales or poses.
invariants.purpose: Tests identity beyond one flattering frame.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated copies of the same pose do not prove stability.

invariants.rule: Give each live phase a different verification duty, including at least one full movement silhouette.
invariants.ablation_failure: Decorative angle changes cannot validate identity.

invariants.rule: Preserve key identity anchors through camera-angle and motion changes.
invariants.ablation_failure: Losing face, silhouette and costume anchors makes the board irrelevant.

invariants.rule: Reserve one late complex skill proof and hold it beside the unchanged board.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on the board alone reads like documentation, not completed live proof.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
